source_evidence.observation: The standing problem is the nonsingular real square system Ax = b with A in R^(n x n) and nonzero b in R^n. [PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, eq. (1.1)]
The paper invokes the standard floating-point model, writes fl(·) for a computed expression, and places hats on computed quantities. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 opening paragraph]

source_evidence.anchor: Section 2, paragraph defining lesssim and approximately-equal; norm and backward-error definitions
source_evidence.observation: The symbols ≲ and ≈ are used after dropping negligible second-order terms. Vector residuals use the 2-norm, matrices use the Frobenius norm where indicated, and the paper's normwise backward error is ||b-A xhat||_2/(||A||_F ||xhat||_2+||b||_2). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 notation and backward-error definition]

The relevant iterative-refinement structure computes r_i=b-Ax_i, solves Ad_i=r_i, and updates x_(i+1)=x_i+d_i. Its computed residual satisfies rhat_i=b-A xhat_i+Delta r_i with ||Delta r_i||_2 <= epsilon_r(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_i||_2). [PDF p. 16, printed p. 1954, Algorithm 2 and eq. (4.1)]

The computed update satisfies xhat_(i+1)=xhat_i+dhat_i+Delta x_i with ||Delta x_i||_2 <= epsilon_u||xhat_(i+1)||_2, and the parameters obey 0 <= epsilon_r, epsilon_u << 1. The paper says epsilon_u is likely the update arithmetic's unit roundoff but deliberately does not require that equality. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 1955, eqs. (4.2)-(4.3) and following discussion]

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Theorem 4.1, iterative-refinement rewrite and paragraph introducing Lemma 4.2
source_evidence.observation: Lemma 4.2 is presented as a generic iterative-refinement result and explicitly does not assume that the correction systems are solved by MOD-GMRES. [PDF p. 18, printed p. 1956, proof of Theorem 4.1 immediately before Lemma 4.2]

For a fixed i >= 0, if nonnegative w_i and omega_i bound the correction residual as in (4.14), then the next true residual satisfies the first-order recurrence (4.15), with Lambda_2^(i)=w_i and lambda_2^(i)=(epsilon_r+epsilon_u+omega_i)(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_(i+1)||_2). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2, eqs. (4.14)-(4.15)]

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (4.18) and the following norm derivation
source_evidence.observation: The proof starts from the exact identity A xhat_(i+1)-b=Delta r_i+A dhat_i-rhat_i+A Delta x_i. It applies (4.1), (4.2), and (4.14), then uses ||xhat_i||_2 ≲ ||xhat_(i+1)||_2 to obtain (4.15). [PDF p. 20, printed p. 1958, eq. (4.18) and immediately following derivation]

binders: First take the nonsingular system Ax=b with A in R^(n x n), nonzero b in R^n, and x in R^n its exact solution. [PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, eq. (1.1)]

Take globally given residual and update accuracy parameters epsilon_r and epsilon_u whose operation models hold for every iterative-refinement index j >= 0. [PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, eqs. (4.1)-(4.3); PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, opening of Lemma 4.2]

For the independent backward branch, fix an iteration i >= 0 and nonnegative scalars w_i and omega_i; they may depend on i. [PDF pp. 19-20, printed pp. 1957-1958, Lemma 4.2 around eq. (4.14) and proof discussion continuing after eq. (4.17)]
hypotheses: Iterative refinement is applied to the nonsingular system (1.1): residual computation, correction-system solution, and solution update have the structure r_i=b-Ax_i, Ad_i=r_i, and x_(i+1)=x_i+d_i. [PDF p. 18, printed p. 1956, proof of Theorem 4.1, three-step iterative-refinement rewrite]
For every j >= 0, rhat_j=b-A xhat_j+Delta r_j and ||Delta r_j||_2 <= epsilon_r(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_j||_2). [PDF p. 16, printed p. 1954, eq. (4.1)]
For every j >= 0, xhat_(j+1)=xhat_j+dhat_j+Delta x_j and ||Delta x_j||_2 <= epsilon_u||xhat_(j+1)||_2. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 1955, eq. (4.2)]
The operation-model parameters satisfy 0 <= epsilon_r, epsilon_u << 1. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 1955, eq. (4.3)]

At the selected index i, the computed correction satisfies ||rhat_i-A dhat_i||_2 <= w_i||b-A xhat_i||_2+omega_i(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_(i+1)||_2), with w_i, omega_i >= 0. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2, eq. (4.14)]

The proof additionally uses ||xhat_i||_2 ≲ ||xhat_(i+1)||_2 when collapsing its exact norm inequality to (4.15); this comparison is proof-side context and is not stated in Lemma 4.2's hypothesis sentence. [PDF p. 20, printed p. 1958, derivation immediately after eq. (4.18); compare PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2]
conclusions: The computed next iterate satisfies ||b-A xhat_(i+1)||_2 ≲ Lambda_2^(i)||b-A xhat_i||_2+lambda_2^(i). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2, eq. (4.15)]
The recurrence coefficients are exactly Lambda_2^(i)=w_i and lambda_2^(i)=(epsilon_r+epsilon_u+omega_i)(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_(i+1)||_2). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2, eq. (4.15)]
definitions_and_conventions: A hat marks a computed quantity; thus xhat_i, rhat_i, and dhat_i are computed iterates, residuals, and corrections. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 opening paragraph; PDF p. 18, printed p. 1956, computed-counterparts paragraph]

For this iterative-refinement section the residual sign convention is b-Ax, even though the introductory GMRES residual is written Ax-b; equations (4.1), (4.14), and (4.15) unambiguously use b-Ax. [PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, paragraph after eq. (1.1); PDF p. 16, printed p. 1954, eq. (4.1); PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eqs. (4.14)-(4.15)]

The expression b-A xhat_i is the unperturbed residual of the computed iterate, whereas rhat_i is the actually computed residual and includes Delta r_i. [PDF p. 16, printed p. 1954, eq. (4.1); PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.14)]

The symbol ≲ denotes a comparison after negligible second-order terms have been dropped; it is not presented as an exact <= relation. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 comparison convention; PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)]
implicit_context: The word 'Independently' separates equations (4.14)-(4.15) from the forward branch (4.12)-(4.13); the multiplicative correction model involving u_i and E_i is not inherited by the selected backward branch. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2 immediately before eq. (4.14)]

The correction dhat_i is the computed output intended to solve the correction system with computed right-hand side Ad_i=rhat_i, but the selected branch requires only its correction-residual bound (4.14). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, opening and independent branch of Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 18, printed p. 1956, generic-solver explanation]
The exact composition underlying the recurrence is A xhat_(i+1)-b=Delta r_i+A dhat_i-rhat_i+A Delta x_i. [PDF p. 20, printed p. 1958, eq. (4.18)]

The indexed scalars w_i and omega_i are allowed to vary between iterations; the lemma is not restricted to repeatedly using one fixed linear solver. [PDF pp. 19-20, printed pp. 1957-1958, proof discussion spanning the page break after eq. (4.17)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Equations (4.14)-(4.15) are the independent residual/backward-error branch for one generic iterative-refinement step: compute a residual, approximately solve the correction system, and update the iterate. The lemma was introduced to analyze restarted MOD-GMRES, but explicitly does not require MOD-GMRES or its basis, preconditioner, and least-squares assumptions. [PDF p. 18, printed p. 1956, iterative-refinement rewrite and paragraph introducing Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2]
numerical_model: The paper invokes the standard floating-point model and identifies hatted variables as computed quantities. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 opening paragraph]
Residual-computation error is modeled normwise by Delta r_i and epsilon_r, covering the matrix-vector product and vector subtraction. [PDF p. 16, printed p. 1954, eq. (4.1) and following sentence]

Update error is modeled normwise by Delta x_i and epsilon_u, covering vector addition; epsilon_u is likely, but is not required to equal, the update precision's unit roundoff. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 1955, eq. (4.2) and following discussion]

The selected models and bound use 2- and Frobenius-norm inequalities rather than the componentwise and infinity-norm assumptions discussed for the earlier Carson-Higham formulation. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, proof discussion after eq. (4.17)]
error_notions: Equation (4.14) controls the absolute 2-norm residual of the correction system, ||rhat_i-A dhat_i||_2. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.14)]
Equation (4.15) is an absolute residual recurrence for ||b-A xhat_i||_2; it is not itself a normalized backward-error inequality. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)]

The associated normwise backward error elsewhere in the paper is ||b-A xhat||_2/(||A||_F||xhat||_2+||b||_2), explaining the scale appearing in (4.14)-(4.15). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, normwise backward-error definition; PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eqs. (4.14)-(4.15)]
norms: Every vector residual and iterate magnitude in (4.1), (4.2), (4.14), and (4.15) uses the Euclidean 2-norm. [PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, eqs. (4.1)-(4.2); PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eqs. (4.14)-(4.15)]

The matrix magnitude multiplying an iterate is ||A||_F, the Frobenius norm, not ||A||_2. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, norm conventions; PDF pp. 16 and 19, printed pp. 1954 and 1957, eqs. (4.1), (4.14), and (4.15)]
constants_and_indexing: The selected step uses current index i and next index i+1; both the correction-bound scale and lambda_2^(i) use ||xhat_(i+1)||_2, while the residual-computation model (4.1) uses ||xhat_i||_2. [PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, eqs. (4.1)-(4.2); PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eqs. (4.14)-(4.15)]
The residual multiplier is exactly Lambda_2^(i)=w_i. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)]
The additive coefficient is exactly epsilon_r+epsilon_u+omega_i, with unit coefficients and no displayed dimension-dependent factor. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)]

Only nonnegativity of w_i and omega_i is required for the one-step statement; no contraction condition w_i<1 is included in equations (4.14)-(4.15). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2 around eqs. (4.14)-(4.15)]
higher_order_terms: Because (4.15) uses ≲, the displayed recurrence is first-order in the paper's convention and has negligible second-order terms omitted. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 comparison convention; PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)]

Before the ≲ step, the proof gives the explicit inequality ||b-A xhat_(i+1)||_2 <= epsilon_r(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_i||_2)+w_i||b-A xhat_i||_2+omega_i(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_(i+1)||_2)+epsilon_u||A||_F||xhat_(i+1)||_2. [PDF p. 20, printed p. 1958, norm derivation following eq. (4.18)]

No explicit big-O expression, numerical remainder bound, or list of the omitted second-order terms accompanies (4.15). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, comparison convention; PDF pp. 19-20, printed pp. 1957-1958, eq. (4.15) and its proof]
exceptional_values: The cited passage gives no explicit overflow, underflow, subnormal, NaN, or infinity assumptions; it models all systems, iterates, and operation errors as real matrices, vectors, and norm bounds while referring only generally to the standard floating-point model. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 opening paragraph; PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, eqs. (4.1)-(4.3)]

undebatable_constraints: The inherited system is real, square, nonsingular, and has nonzero right-hand side: A in R^(n x n), 0 != b in R^n. [PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, eq. (1.1)]
The selected result is the independent branch (4.14)-(4.15), not the forward branch (4.12)-(4.13). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2, word 'Independently' before eq. (4.14)]

Conditions (4.1)-(4.3) on computed residuals and updates are inherited assumptions of the selected branch. [PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, eqs. (4.1)-(4.3); PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, opening of Lemma 4.2]
The correction hypothesis must retain both terms in (4.14): w_i times the current unperturbed residual and omega_i times ||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_(i+1)||_2. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.14)]

The correction bound concerns rhat_i-A dhat_i, where rhat_i is computed, while its right-hand side uses b-A xhat_i, the unperturbed residual expression. [PDF p. 16, printed p. 1954, eq. (4.1); PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.14)]

The conclusion must retain the complete two-term recurrence and the exact definitions Lambda_2^(i)=w_i and lambda_2^(i)=(epsilon_r+epsilon_u+omega_i)(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_(i+1)||_2). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)]
The vector norm is the 2-norm and the matrix norm in the scale is the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, norm conventions; PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eqs. (4.14)-(4.15)]

The conclusion uses ≲ rather than exact <= and therefore carries the paper's dropped-second-order convention. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, comparison convention; PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)]

The proof-side exact identity (4.18) and the comparison ||xhat_i||_2 ≲ ||xhat_(i+1)||_2 are part of the derivational context for (4.15). [PDF p. 20, printed p. 1958, eq. (4.18) and following norm derivation]
No MOD-GMRES-specific basis, preconditioner, or least-squares hypothesis belongs to Lemma 4.2's generic selected branch. [PDF p. 18, printed p. 1956, paragraph introducing Lemma 4.2]

ambiguities.issue: The proof invokes ||xhat_i||_2 ≲ ||xhat_(i+1)||_2, but this comparison is not listed in the formal hypothesis sentence of Lemma 4.2. [PDF p. 20, printed p. 1958, derivation after eq. (4.18); compare PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, Lemma 4.2]
ambiguities.evidence: The page-20 proof explicitly says 'considering' this iterate comparison before deriving the displayed ≲ bound, whereas the selected branch on page 19 states only (4.14), nonnegativity of w_i and omega_i, and the inherited conditions (4.1)-(4.3). [PDF pp. 19-20, printed pp. 1957-1958, eqs. (4.14)-(4.18)]
ambiguities.impact: A literal formalization must decide whether to add the comparison as a premise, derive it from additional iterative-refinement context, or retain a more detailed inequality involving ||xhat_i||_2; silently omitting it would not reproduce the printed proof. [PDF p. 20, printed p. 1958, norm derivation after eq. (4.18)]

ambiguities.issue: The relation ≲ is not quantitatively defined beyond dropping 'negligible second order terms.' [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 comparison convention]
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (4.15) contains no explicit remainder, asymptotic variable, or bound for the omitted terms. [PDF pp. 19-20, printed pp. 1957-1958, eq. (4.15) and its proof]
ambiguities.impact: The source does not authorize replacing ≲ by an exact <= with the same right-hand side unless an external formal interpretation of the omitted terms is supplied. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, comparison convention; PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)]

ambiguities.issue: The parameters epsilon_r and epsilon_u are not tied to a single specified arithmetic precision or exact unit-roundoff formula. [PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, eqs. (4.1)-(4.3) and discussion after eq. (4.2)]
ambiguities.evidence: The paper calls them magnitude-bounding parameters and says epsilon_u is 'very likely' the update unit roundoff while explicitly allowing other outcomes. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 1955, paragraph after eq. (4.2)]
ambiguities.impact: A contract must keep epsilon_r and epsilon_u abstract rather than hard-code epsilon_u=u or assume residual and update computations use the same precision. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 1955, discussion after eq. (4.2)]

ambiguities.issue: Exceptional floating-point values and range failures are not explicitly addressed in the selected passage. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, standard-model reference; PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, operation models]
ambiguities.evidence: The paper states real-valued norm models but gives no local clause excluding overflow, underflow, subnormals, NaNs, or infinities. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, Section 2 opening paragraph; PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, eqs. (4.1)-(4.3)]
ambiguities.impact: The selected claim should be understood only under the stated real-valued error models; behavior involving exceptional values cannot be recovered from this passage. [PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 1954-1955, eqs. (4.1)-(4.3)]

contract_plain_english: For one iteration of generic iterative refinement on the nonsingular real system Ax=b, assume the computed residual and update satisfy the normwise models (4.1)-(4.3), and assume the computed correction residual is bounded by (4.14) with nonnegative w_i and omega_i. [PDF pp. 16-19, printed pp. 1954-1957, eqs. (4.1)-(4.3) and (4.14)] Then the next unperturbed residual obeys the first-order recurrence ||b-A xhat_(i+1)||_2 ≲ w_i||b-A xhat_i||_2+(epsilon_r+epsilon_u+omega_i)(||b||_2+||A||_F||xhat_(i+1)||_2). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 1957, eq. (4.15)] This branch is independent of the lemma's forward-error branch and of MOD-GMRES-specific assumptions, but its printed proof additionally uses the unstated comparison ||xhat_i||_2 ≲ ||xhat_(i+1)||_2 and the paper's convention of dropping negligible second-order terms. [PDF p. 18, printed p. 1956, paragraph introducing Lemma 4.2; PDF pp. 19-20, printed pp. 1957-1958, independent branch and derivation after eq. (4.18); PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, comparison convention]
